whatTheCounterMeans: Every literal field value in places.json is looked for in the evidence bytes of the source its record cites. UNKNOWN means the value appears in NO captured source. It is explicitly 'not a failure by itself' — the failure the gate exists for is ABSENT (present in a source, but not the cited one) and NEAR-VARIANT (differs from the cited source by a digit).
decisionRule: Classify, never fill. A value with no source is one of two things and the fix differs. (a) OSM-DERIVED: the value IS in the cited source, but as a tag fragment rather than the composed string the record stored — fix by storing the source's own literal. (b) CURATED: our translation or our own label; no source can exist — keep the value, say so, and close the guide's verified-column gate on it, because a name we wrote must not print behind 'we verified this'. The forbidden move is inventing a citation to make the counter go down: that is the exact defect this project exists to prevent, and it is worth less than an honest UNKNOWN.

entries.valueBefore: 京都市下京区四条通烏丸東入長刀鉾町8
entries.why: OSM carries the address as four separate tags (addr:province 京都府, addr:city 京都市, addr:suburb 下京区, addr:quarter 長刀鉾町, addr:block_number 8). No single tag contains the joined string, so whole-string containment cannot match and never will. Every FRAGMENT is the source's; the composition (ward order, the join) is ours.
entries.action: Declared as a composition in place record's addressProvenance, and the traditional street-and-entry clause 四条通烏丸東入 was REMOVED because no source read for this pack contains it. Storing a plausible-looking street clause would have been an invented address fragment.

entries.why: OSM way/105449683 name:en=West Tower Gate. The shrine name was our prefix. This one mattered twice: because the record's source_url pointed at the shrine's Japanese access page, which contains no English at all, the value appeared in no source the gate could reach — an ABSENT, not merely an UNKNOWN, once the prefix was corrected.
entries.action: nameEn set to the OSM tag verbatim AND the record's source_url repointed to the OSM element, because a citation must name a source that can carry the value. The shrine's page is still declared in sourcesByField for the fields it does carry.

entries.why: OSM way/88108397 name:en=Main Shrine. 'Main Hall (Honden)' was our rendering.

note: No entry in this table was resolved by adding a citation. Eight were resolved by making our value equal the source's own literal (we had been appending editorial words to sourced names); two are ours and are now labelled as ours with the guide gate closed; two are compositions whose fragments are the source's and whose joining is ours. The remaining UNKNOWN count of 4 is the honest floor for this pack: two composed addresses and two labels for OSM objects that carry no name tag.
